title: Marketplace entry scripts + runtime fallback checklist (draft)
body:
Purpose:
This doc collects: 1) curated microcopy and short scripts for marketplace tiles, hero blurbs, and trial CTAs, and 2) an operational checklist and runbook for runtime fallbacks (what to do when a listing's preferred deployment or model variant is unavailable).

Background / context notes (brief):
- Many partner listings fail late because copy + UX assume the hosted API always wins. we need copy variants that explicitly show compatibility with Dedicated and Private modes and a graceful UX when features are restricted (e.g., no streaming, limited region).
- Ops has seen a handful of incidents where customers hit capacity for a popular model variant; the tile flow currently surfaces a vague "temporarily unavailable". We want deterministic messaging and an automated fallback plan to avoid conversion loss.

Target audiences:
- Partner product & growth teams (copy clarity)
- Marketplace ops / GTM (acceptance gates)
- Engineering + Runtime (fallback policies & telemetry)

1) Entry scripts and microcopy (short, user-facing strings)
- Tile headline (primary): "Redwood Inference — predictable LLM inference for apps"
- Tile headline (alternate shorter): "Prod-ready LLM inference"
- 1-line descriptor (trial tile): "Try hosted inference with low-latency defaults — no infra required."
- 1-line descriptor (enterprise tile): "Dedicated GPU pools and private deployment options for regulated data."
- Hero blurb (longer): "Ship LLM features without guesswork: fast inference, cost controls, and the same API across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Try a live demo or request a dedicated capacity trial."
- CTA primary: "Start free trial" (when hosted available)
- CTA alt for enterprise: "Request dedicated trial"
- CTA when Hosted unavailable but Dedicated exists: "Request dedicated access — regionally available"
- Info tooltip copy for limitations: "Limited features: streaming and certain model variants disabled on this plan. See details in the plan comparison."
- Error / unavailable microcopy (friendly): "This configuration isn’t available in your region right now. We can route you to a compatible model or reserve dedicated capacity — click to choose."
- Button for fallback choice: "Show compatible options"

Copy variants for trial conversion experiments (A/B):
A: "Start free trial — includes 30k tokens, sample prompts, and live latency metrics."
B: "Try Redwood hosted API — 30k free tokens, no credit card for the first 7 days."
C: "Preview in your region — automated routing to the nearest compatible runtime."

Localization notes (to translation team):
- Keep CTAs short (2–3 words) where possible. Use neutral verbs.
- For EU/DE/FR locales add an inline hint when Dedicated or Private is recommended for data residency.

2) Acceptance checklist for marketplace listing (pre-publish)
- Copy & UX: final hero blurb, tile headline, 2 CTAs (trial + enterprise) included and approved.
- Billing: SKU defined in billing catalog, test purchase flow from sandbox, metering labels match SKU.
- Security: SSO/SAML instructions attached, KMS integration notes if Private deploy supported.
- Legal: Data residency/processing statement included if listing targets EU/health verticals.
- Tech gating: sample API key for sandbox, example request/response in tile details, streaming example (if supported).
- Telemetry hooks: page_load, tile_cta_click, start_trial_submitted, fallback_choice_selected instrumented and validated in staging.
- Capacity: guaranteed Dedicated capacity documented (if selling reserved), and expected latency SLOs listed.
- Support: support contact and escalation path included; success playbook (30/60/90) present for co-sell.
- Accessibility: hero copy & CTA pass contrast and screenreader readout sanity check.

Publish decision flow (quick):
- If Hosted + Dedicated + Private all supported: publish with full CTAs.
- If Hosted supported but streaming disabled: publish but surface feature hint and show streaming example as "Coming soon".
- If Hosted NOT supported but Dedicated exists: hide "Start free trial" and surface "Request dedicated trial" + region availability.
- If only Private: listing should be gated as "Enterprise — contact sales", include deployment checklist.

3) Runtime fallback policy (ops + runtime engineering)
Goal: avoid dead-end UX when preferred model/deployment is unavailable and preserve conversions.
Fallback tiers (preferred -> fallback):
- Tier 0: Preferred model variant on Hosted instance (low-latency kernel, streaming enabled).
- Tier 1: Compatible model variant on Hosted (quantized or smaller-size model) — show minor quality caveat.
- Tier 2: Dedicated pool equivalent (if partner/account has dedicated commit) — may require request/approval.
- Tier 3: Private deployment contact — offer sales outreach.

Automated behaviors to implement (notes for engineering):
- When Tier 0 unavailable for a new trial request, attempt Tier 1 automatically for first request, but show a banner: "Using a compatible model to keep things fast — results may differ slightly."
- If Tier 1 latency > threshold (200ms/token median) for N=3 requests, present modal to user with 2 choices: "Switch to dedicated trial" or "Continue with degraded performance." Capture choice.
- If Tier 2 exists for the tenant, present "Request dedicated access" button that opens a pre-filled form (tenant id, requested qps, target latency).
- Always log fallback_reason with tags: model_variant, region, capacity_tier, requested_qps.

User-facing fallback messaging principles:
- Be explicit about the change and its impact (quality, latency).
- Offer an action (switch to dedicated, try a different model) rather than a dead-end message.
- Keep language short and not overly technical.

4) Operational runbook (abbreviated)
- Incident: "listing fallback rate > 10% for a 24h window"
  - Triage owner: marketplace-ops oncall (pager duty link in linked_artifacts).
  - Immediate step: Check model capacity dashboard (redwood console -> per-model capacity).
  - If capacity exhausted on Hosted: trigger automated routing to Tier 1 for new requests and post an in-product banner.
  - If Tier 1 also degraded: open high-priority support ticket and notify sales & partner success.
  - Postmortem owner: eng-serving-runtime + marketplace-ops.

- Incident: "purchase/trial provisioning failing for specific SKU"
  - Triage: confirm billing SKU mapping and sandbox purchase logs.
  - Rollback: temporarily disable trial CTA and surface "Contact sales" until fix.

5) Telemetry & instrumentation (key signals)
- page_load_ts, tile_impression, tile_cta_click, start_trial_attempt, trial_provision_success, fallback_triggered, fallback_choice_selected, trial_conversion_rate_by_tile_variant, region_latency_histogram.
- Alerts to set (ops): fallback_triggered rate > 5% sustained for 1h; trial_provision_failure_rate > 2% for 30m.

6) Sample short copy snippets for partner docs & email nurture
- "Thanks for listing with Redwood — your marketplace tile is live in staging. Quick checklist: confirm SKU, confirm billing sandbox purchase, confirm SSO docs. Reply here when ready for publish."
- Behavioral email (when fallback triggered for a customer): "Heads up — we routed requests to a compatible model to keep your app responsive. We recommend requesting a dedicated trial if you need consistent latency. Click to request."

7) Open questions / TODOs
- Who will own the final "fallback UX" mocks? (need designer + runtime engineer).
- Localization lead to confirm translations for DE/FR/JP CTAs.
- Confirm the exact latency thresholds for auto-switch (suggest: median token latency > 200ms triggers modal).
- Decide whether to expose a "quality slider" (user chooses smaller/faster model) in tile details — privacy/security implications?

Next steps (near-term):
- Maya to spin up a staging tile with the new CTA variants (A/B) by 2026-03-04.
- Jasper to prototype the fallback banner and event payloads for telemetry by 2026-03-11.
- Claire to run a legal check for EU data residency blurb by 2026-03-09.

Slack refs / quick links (for internal reviewers):
- #marketplace-ops, #partner-success, #eng-hosted-api.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally prescriptive — we want a deterministic publish flow and clear messaging for fallbacks to protect conversion. Treat copy as experiment variants; final strings will be trimmed by localization.

End of doc.
